name: Ding Wenchao
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Scientist, TARS (它石智航), Shanghai embodied-AI/robotics company
profile: Ding Wenchao joined Huawei in 2020 as one of its 'Genius Youth' recruits and worked on the decision-making network for its ADS 1.0 intelligent-driving system. In 2023 he became a researcher at Fudan University, then co-founded TARS in 2025 with Chen Yilun and Li Zhenyu. As chief scientist he leads TARS's AWE foundation model and DexHand dexterous hand.
interesting_fact: MIT Technology Review named him to its 2025 Innovators Under 35 China list (Inventor category), and he gave a plenary keynote at ICRA 2026 in Vienna.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and did his graduate degree at HKUST; at Fudan he developed the university's first humanoid robot.
notes: The Fudan humanoid-robot detail is from Gasgoo (https://autonews.gasgoo.com/articles/news/seeds-former-huawei-and-baidu-executives-team-up-secure-over-3-billion-yuan-in-financing-2044746801104470017); education is from cnyes. Most technical and English-friendly of the TARS founders, so a good podcast guest.

name: Robert Krayn
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Talkiatry (New York telepsychiatry company)
profile: Robert Krayn left a finance career in 2019 to co-found Talkiatry with psychiatrist Dr. Georgia Gaveras. It is an in-network virtual psychiatry and therapy practice that employs its clinicians as salaried staff. Talkiatry went fully virtual during COVID and grew to 800+ psychiatrists; it raised a $210M Series D in Feb 2026, bringing total funding past $400M.
interesting_fact: Talkiatry planned to see patients in person, with its first appointment set for April 2020 in New York, but lockdown forced it to go fully virtual, which became the basis of its growth.
deep_cut_fact: A Rutgers alum who worked in finance, Krayn made Business Insider's 2023 '30 leaders under 40 changing healthcare' list at age 35, recognized for running Talkiatry as a better workplace for psychiatrists.
notes: He has spoken publicly about struggling to find in-network psychiatric care himself; that is the founding story, but handle it with care and don't use it as an outreach hook. Talkiatry's press page also has a downloadable press kit.

name: Xiao Wenpeng
current_role: Listed by Hurun as founder of xTool (Shenzhen laser engraver / maker-tools company); title not verified
profile: Hurun's 2026 unicorn list names Xiao Wenpeng as founder of xTool, a Shenzhen maker of desktop laser engravers and cutters, UV printers and the xTool Studio software, valued at about $1B. We could not independently verify his biography or title.
interesting_fact: xTool donates 1% of its net profits to give maker tools to schools, nonprofits and makerspaces ('1% for the Makers'), and has won multiple Red Dot and iF design awards.
notes: Web search budget ran out before this person, so identity and bio are unverified. xTool's site lists only customer-support and purchase-order emails, no press contact. Re-research recommended (Chinese-language sources, any HKEX prospectus).
